correctness.rationale: For all integers n>=3 and every real gamma>0, the 2n nonparallel weighted incidence vectors are exactly the oriented generators of exposed zonotope edges, so a linear isometry must permute them with signs and preserve triangle dependencies. For n>=4 the triangle incidence counts (2 per spoke, 1 per rim edge) force spoke preservation and hence one signed dihedral coordinate permutation; for n=3 and gamma!=1 the unique equal-coefficient circuit forces the same conclusion. For n=3 gamma=1 all four triangle circuits are symmetric, their incidence permutation is at most S4, and the explicit reanchoring action realizes S4, with a further independent global sign. The edge and coefficient arguments prove completeness, not merely a lower bound. Exact rational enumerations recover orders 12,48,12 and 16,16,16 in six sample cases; 5840 successful finite assertions do not establish the general theorem.

originality.rationale: No inspected statement gave the complete all-n/all-positive-gamma isometry classification or the unique tetrahedral enhancement. Hamad proves a continuous Euclidean Sobolev W^{k,1} theorem, Cúth--Doucha--Titkos prove isometries for Lipschitz-free graph spaces and dual max-Lipschitz norms rather than the additive graph variation norm, and Padrol--Pilaud--Poullot describe deformations of graphical zonotopes rather than their weighted norm isometry groups. Nearest published-finding corpus records deal with unrelated graph variation max-norm facets, metrics on wheel graphs, or hyperplane cube isometry moduli. Graphic-matroid automorphism theorems may imply a reformulation, so the PASS is best knowledge, not an absolute uniqueness claim.

value.rationale: This is a complete and naturally motivated classification of the intrinsic linear symmetries of first-order ℓ1 graph-Sobolev norms on every finite cycle. It detects a unique exact dimension/weight point where vertex penalties and edge-gradient penalties become interchangeable under tetrahedral reanchoring, producing a sharp group order jump 12 to 48; the effect disappears immediately under any positive weight perturbation. This identifies the boundary of discrete rigidity, not an arbitrary parameter slice or textbook substitution.
